title: Windows state files inherit the parent directory DACL
description: At 8d714a201280318f92ed42d26d20bf233a1f5baf the attacker starts as a second local Windows account that can open files under its own token. That account is not the creating user, is not a member of Administrators, and is not SYSTEM or an elevated token. Those two principals are comparable to root, which can already read the Unix 0600 files. The OS principal boundary is that second account's token against the creating user's state files. On Unix, tsk forces the state directory to 0700 and task files such as tsk.json to 0600 so another local user cannot read task data. On Windows, ensure_private_dir, create_private_file, and tighten_file set no security descriptor and no mode: a missing state directory is created with create_dir_all, and tsk.json is opened with OpenOptions that apply mode 0600 only under cfg(unix). tighten_file is a no-op off Unix, including on later load, so this repository never narrows a Windows DACL after creation. src/fsperm.rs and src/store.rs are unchanged from b5b92d60 through this commit, and the cited lines still match. The header comment that no permission is claimed off Unix does not show whether the inherited parent DACL already excludes that second account. The installer creates %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\tsk\bin and does not create or ACL the state directory. A second non-admin local account might read %LOCALAPPDATA%\tsk\tsk.json if that inherited DACL allows it. Plaintext readable only by the creating account would not cross this boundary. Source cannot show the inherited DACL.
claimed_root_cause: ensure_private_dir, create_private_file, and tighten_file apply owner-only mode bits only on Unix. On Windows they create the state directory and task files through std::fs with no security descriptor and never call a DACL API, so the directory and tsk.json keep the parent directory's inherited DACL and are not tightened later.

trace.description: When TSK_STATE_DIR is unset and LOCALAPPDATA is non-empty, the Windows default is that directory joined with tsk. Lines 1401-1403 return PathBuf::from(local).join("tsk"). Lines 1406-1408 fall back to USERPROFILE joined with .tsk when LOCALAPPDATA is empty.
Each supported save calls ensure_private_dir on the state directory at line 793, then tighten_state_files at line 795, before replacing tsk.json.
A missing directory is created with fs::create_dir_all. The Windows-only extra step is reject_reparse_ancestors at lines 35-36. tighten_private_dir, which applies 0700, is cfg(unix) at lines 55-56.

Each existing private state name, including tsk.json, is passed to tighten_file at line 1156. Load at line 714 and save at line 795 both call this function, so a later load is the same no-op off Unix.
The cfg(not(unix)) body at lines 300-303 discards the path. No mode bits and no security descriptor are written.

The temp document is opened with filesystem.create_file. StdFilesystem::create_file at line 284 calls create_private_file. tighten_state_files has already returned at line 795 and does not run again after this create.
OpenOptions is write, create, and truncate at line 175, then open. mode(0o600) exists only inside cfg(unix) at lines 176-179. The Windows open passes no security descriptor.

evidence.description: The module header says Unix state directories are 0700 and files are 0600, and that no permission is claimed on other platforms, where these helpers compile down to plain create and copy.
Before create_dir_all, Windows only calls reject_reparse_ancestors. The directory create attaches no security descriptor.
The directory tighten call is gated by cfg(unix); the Windows function returns after the reparse and directory checks.
options.mode(0o600) is inside the cfg(unix) block that begins at line 176.
Under cfg(not(unix)), tighten_file ignores its path. An existing Windows state file is not given an owner-only DACL.
The production AtomicFilesystem create_file implementation is create_private_file, with no Windows security-attribute argument.
Load calls tighten_state_files, which is a no-op off Unix.
The non-empty LOCALAPPDATA branch returns PathBuf::from(local).join("tsk").
When LOCALAPPDATA is unavailable, the Windows fallback returns PathBuf::from(userprofile).join(".tsk").
The storage guide documents the Windows default as LOCALAPPDATA\tsk, or USERPROFILE\.tsk when LOCALAPPDATA is unavailable, and does not document a Windows ACL. This line is unchanged since b5b92d60.
The Windows installer default directory is LOCALAPPDATA joined with Programs\tsk\bin. That is the program directory, not the state directory.
The installer creates that program directory with New-Item. The repository contains no DACL, icacls, or Set-Acl call, so the installer does not ACL the state directory.

blockers: The inherited DACL is an operating-system fact. This repository never sets or records a Windows security descriptor, so source cannot show whether a second non-admin account, which is not the owner and not Administrators or SYSTEM, has an allow ACE.
A Windows DACL observation is required and was not performed. This host is Linux, so it cannot create a Windows profile or query a DACL, and target code was not executed.

validation_plan.local: On a fresh Windows 10 or 11 profile that is not a member of Administrators and is not elevated, leave TSK_STATE_DIR unset and do not pass --state-dir. Run tsk add with a dummy title so the default state directory and tsk.json are created. As that same user, run icacls with only the path, and no /grant, /deny, /remove, /reset, /setowner, /inheritance, /restore, or /replace, on %LOCALAPPDATA%\tsk and on %LOCALAPPDATA%\tsk\tsk.json and record every ACE and inheritance flag. If LOCALAPPDATA was unset, use %USERPROFILE%\.tsk instead. From a second local account that is also not a member of Administrators, not SYSTEM, and not elevated, attempt only to read those two paths and stop at access denied or at seeing the dummy text. Do not take ownership, change the ACL, or use an elevated token. If that second account can read the dummy text, the boundary the Unix build enforces with 0700 and 0600 is crossed. If access is denied and the DACL allows only the creating user, SYSTEM, and Administrators, the inherited DACL already matches that account boundary.
validation_plan.deployment: On an existing Windows store, run icacls with only the path on the state directory and on tsk.json. Do not change the ACL, do not take ownership, and do not open the task file. Record whether any allow ACE, including an inherited ACE, grants read to a principal other than the owner, SYSTEM, and Administrators. Stop after recording the DACL.
